sentences.text: He has submitted that while granting compensation under the heads of pain, shock and suffering, the Tribunal has also included compensation of loss of amenities and expectation of life together with physical and mental pain, which is impermissible.
It is submitted that the Tribunal has also erred in granting Rs.3,00,000/- towards the future medical treatment and Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical expenses with interest @ 9% per month.
He has further submitted that the Tribunal has also determined the prospective income of Rs.6,000/- erroneously and instead, it should be Rs.5,600/- per month.

Finally, it is submitted that the claimant has already passed away on 03.10.2018 and hence, while placing reliance on the judgement of this Court dated 15.12.2015 passed in First Appeal No.1528 of 2009, he has submitted that the compensation is required to be reduced.
3.

Per contra, learned advocate Mr.Bhalodi appearing for the claimant has submitted that the deceased was a driver and in fact, his income was required to be considered as per the Minimum Wages Act, 1948 however, the Tribunal has not considered the same.
It is submitted that thus, the actual income as well as prospective income, as derived by the Tribunal, does not require interference.

He has submitted that the deceased C/FA/157/2018 ORDER DATED: 20/03/2023 was 95% disabled and was a paraplegic patient and due to his injuries, he passed away during the pendency of the first appeals.
It is thus submitted that the judgement, on which the reliance is placed by the learned advocate Mr.Nanavati cannot come to his rescue and compensation is not required to be reduced.

He has further submitted that so far as the award of compensation under the heads of pain, shock and suffering is concerned, it is submitted that the same is appropriately awarded as Rs.8,00,000/- looking to the 95% disability of the deceased.
Thus, it is submitted that the impugned judgement and decree is not required to be interfered with.

4. Learned advocate Mr.Parikh appearing for ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company (First Appeal No.47 of 2018) has submitted that the findings of the Tribunal with regard to holding the truck driver as 20% negligent in causing the accident are required to be quashed since the evidence reveals that in fact, the driver of the motor car having registration No.GJ-10-BG-545 was coming from wrong side on a four lane high-way having divider.
Thus, it is submitted that the motor car driver can be held 100% negligent for the accident.
Thus, it is urged that the appellant-Insurance Company is required to be absolved of holding the truck driver as 20% negligent for the accident.
This Court has perused the evidences, which are surfaced on record as well as in the impugned judgement and order.
A vehicular accident occurred on 05.06.2013 at 00:30 AM night on Upleta Bypass, Rajkot-Porbandar National Highway.
The accident had occurred between truck having registration No.GJ-03-AT-1824 and the motor car having registration No.GJ-10-BG-545.
Due to the aforesaid accident, the claimant suffered 95% disability and was paraplegic.

After considering both,
oral as well as documentary evidences, the Tribunal has awarded the aforesaid amount as compensation.
6. The evidence on record reveals that the appellant/claimant was 33 years old and was a driver.
It was asserted by the claimant that he was earning Rs.9,000/- per month however, due to the lack of National Insurance Company Ltd., ... vs Decd. Prafulbhai Premjibhai Radiya ...

2 evidence, the Tribunal has fixed income as Rs.4,000/- per month and by adding 50% future prospective income, the total income was determined as Rs.6,000/- per month.
We are of the opinion that income of the claimant is appropriately determined at Rs.4,000/- per month and accordingly, prospective income of Rs.6,000/- also does not require any interference.
It is also not in dispute that the claimant had suffered injuries and he was paraplegic and was aged about 33/32 years.
During pendency of the C/FA/157/2018 ORDER DATED: 20/03/2023 first appeals, the claimant passed away on 03.10.2018.

7. It is the case of the appellant that the amount of compensation is required to be reduced since he was passed away and reliance is placed on the judgement dated 15.12.2015 passed in First Appeal No.1528 of 2009 in this regard.

We have perused the aforesaid judgement and on a perusal of the same, it reveals that it will not affect the compensation determined by the Tribunal in view of the facts of the present case, wherein the claimant has passed away due to his injuries.

The claimant was totally bed ridden, whereas in the case in the said judgement, which is cited before this Court, the claimant had passed away due to natural cause and hence, this Court had re-determined the compensation, which was awarded towards the future loss of income.
Thus, the amount of compensation cannot be reduced in wake of the fact that the death has resulted due to the serious injuries suffered by him in the accident.

8. So far as the contention raised by the appellant of awarding the compensation of Rs.8,00,000/-
under the heads of pain, shock and suffering is concerned, the same does not merit acceptance.

It is the case of the appellant that the amount under the heads of pain, shock and C/FA/157/2018 ORDER DATED: 20/03/2023 suffering of Rs.2,00,000/- was not required to be determined and awarded since he has already awarded further amount of Rs.3,00,000/- for loss of amenities and expectation of life and further awarded Rs.3,00,00/- for physical and mental pain.

Such contention is required to be rejected out-rightly since even if it is presumed that such amounts are not added separately and awarded under the heads of pain, shock and suffering, the amount of Rs.2,00,000/-
awarded by the Tribunal would be a very meager amount looking to the injuries suffered by the claimant.
Thus, the amount of total Rs.8,00,000/- as determined by the Tribunal under the heads of pain, shock and suffering is appropriate and reasonable.

Merely because the Tribunal has sub-categorized the heads under pain, shock and suffering, the same itself would not be a factor to reduce the amount of compensation since the claimant, who subsequently passed away, was paraplegic.
Thus, this Court is of the opinion that the amount of compensation as awarded by the Tribunal does not require any interference.

9. Further issue, which falls for deliberation before this Court is whether the Tribunal has appropriately held the negligence on the part of the truck driver to the extent of 20% in causing the accident.

The evidence, which has surfaced and established from the record more particularly, the contents of the F.I.R. (below Exh.29) as well as Panchnama of scene of occurrence (below Exh.30)
and the deposition of the owner of the truck (below Exh.31) if are read together, the same would National Insurance Company Ltd., ... vs Decd.
Prafulbhai Premjibhai Radiya ...

on 20 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/172713695/
3 reveal that the accident has occurred on a four lane national highway having a divider.
The driver of the car, despite there being a divider, was travelling in a wrong direction, whereas the truck driver was on the right side.
Thus, the car driver was supposed not to drive in a wrong lane, which was meant for the ongoing vehicles like the truck that too on four lane highway having divider.

The accident has occurred at midnight and hence, the driver of the motor car would be solely responsible for the accident and the truck driver cannot be held responsible to any extent for the accident.
The evidence also reveals that the truck driver on seeing the car coming from the opposite direction in wrong a lane had taken his truck on the left side however, the motor car dashed with the truck.

11. Under the circumstances, the Tribunal has fallen in error in holding the truck driver as 20%
negligent for the cause of accident.

Thus, liability of the appellant-Insurance Company of First Appeal No.47 of 2018 i.e. ICICI Lombard General Insurance Company is shifted to the C/FA/157/2018 ORDER DATED: 20/03/2023 appellant-Insurance Company of First Appeal No.157 of 2018 i.e. National Insurance Company.
12. Accordingly, the impugned judgement and decree is modified to the aforesaid extent only.
An amount, which is lying in the form of FDR before the Tribunal shall be disbursed to the heirs of the claimant, after due verification with the accrued interest.
12. First Appeal No.157 of 2018 stands dismissed and First Appeal No.47 of 2018 is allowed.
The connected civil application accordingly stands disposed of.
R & P to be sent back.
Registry to place a copy of this order in the connected matter.
